name: Aragonese Infantry
author: mylae
description: [Medieval 2 Total War - Machiavello mod](http://www.twcenter.net/forums/forumdisplay.php?2240-Machiavello-Total-War-(MachTW)) | Model for an Aragonese Infantry. Around mid-XV century, a number of Iberian soldiers followed [Alfonso V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_V_of_Aragon) in his conquest of the Kingdom of Naples. They usually had a shield - usually an [Adarga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adarga) - a couple of javelins and a lance, as well as a sword or knife, and on the head a hat, cap or helmet. Contemporary sources depicts them with brigandine or haubergeon, sometime having pieces of leg armour, relatively lightly armoured in respect to heavier Italian counterparts, but more dedicated to a proactive assault role, forerunner of the sword-and-buckler infantry later developed in Spain.

name: Dutch Ship Medium
author: Console Art Cybernetic
description: **Dutch Ship Medium** is a detailed mid-scale 3D sailing vessel inspired by classic Dutch maritime design, crafted for historical, adventure, and naval-themed environments. It features a realistic wooden hull, structured sails, and authentic deck details, making it ideal for games, cinematics, and environment showcases. Built with optimized geometry (around 69k triangles) and high-quality 2K textures, the model balances visual fidelity and performance for real-time engines like **Unity** and **Godot**. Its modular and game-ready structure makes it suitable for open-sea scenes, pirate settings, or historical world-building projects.

name: Chiesa di San Grato a Sala Monferrato
author: Giorgio Scioldo
description: Church of San Grato in Sala Monferrato. The religious building was built in the mid-17th century as a votive offering after a plague and to ask for protection from hail. According to popular memory, the entire Salesian population contributed to the construction of the church, forming a human chain which, from the town's brickyard, allowed the transport of the bricks to the chosen site. Already in the mid-18th century, a complete restoration was necessary by Scapitta, the main exponent of Piedmontese Baroque, and financed through the sale of local agricultural products. In 1771 the painter Pietro Guala created the image of San Grato in the dome and the four cardinal virtues. Over the years the church fell into disuse and the structural conditions worsened, making the building unsafe. In 1998 a group of Salesian volunteers began working on the recovery of the building: the roof was renovated and the churchyard was recovered, to bring the church back to its original beauty. (Source: www.ilmonferrato.it)

name: Clifford Williams Tombstone
author: Abby Crawford
description: From the Santa Cruz Sentinel, August 4, 1866: "Clifford Williams, a coal-passer of the man of war Suwanee, died on board Monday, July 30, 1866. He was buried on Tuesday in the Santa Cruz cemetery by the officers and men of the steamer, with appropriate honors.... It was most commendable on the part of the commander of the Suwanee, to put in here and give the poor fellow a Christian burial in a Christian cemetery, and goes to prove that there are some ship captains who are not lost to all feelings of humanity. The procession presented a very fine appearance as they passed through the town, upon their melancholy errand.... Deceased was 25 years of age...." The Suwanee was a Union ship commissioned in 1864. It sailed from Philadelphia early in 1865 and headed down the American East Coast to intercept Confederate pirates. After traveling to the tip of South America, the ship headed north along the Pacific coast and was eventually wrecked off the northwest part of Vancouver Island, British Columbia, in 1868.

name: Casa de Braganca
author: VirtualPhoto3D
description: The Most Serene House of Braganza, also known as the Brigantine dynasty, is a noble family of Portuguese origin that produced emperors, kings, princes, and dukes who ruled in both Europe and the Americas. Founded by Afonso I, the 1st Duke of Braganza and the illegitimate son of King John I of Portugal from the House of Aviz, the house grew to become one of the wealthiest and most influential noble families in Iberia during the Renaissance. The Braganza family rose to power by overthrowing the Philippine Dynasty in the Restoration War, leading to the Duke of Braganza ascending to the throne as King John IV of Portugal in 1640. The Braganzas then ruled Portugal and its empire from 1640 onward. With the establishment of the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil, and the Algarves in 1815, and Brazil's independence in 1822, the Braganza family also became monarchs of Brazil. Location: Guimaraes, Portugal Photogrammetry Capture Method: DJI Mini2

name: Salegs Revenge

description: Salegs Revenge is a steam ship of the line which would have been produced during the early - late 1850's, and whithin the lore of Mellisay she stands as the last age of sail ship before the plunge into the ironclad era. The construction would likely be a hybrid of iron frames and supports with the rest being wood, to ensure more durabillity, alongside posessing a basic steam engine for auxillery propulsion.

name: Echoes of the Deep - galleon
author: Brian Trepanier
description: Anchored in time and salt, an old galleon rests beneath a dusky sky, sails still catching the wind as if waiting for one last voyage. Its wood, dark with centuries of sun and sea, groans softly with each wave, telling stories few remember. This ship once ruled the oceans—three masts rising high, sails billowing with purpose. It carried treasures, crewed by sailors chasing maps and myths. The deck, now empty, once echoed with boots and shouted orders. Cannons still sit along the sides, silent but ready, rust creeping over cold iron. Seagulls circle above, and the sea hums below, wrapping the vessel in memory. Whether lost in battle, storm, or forgotten port, the galleon remains—proud, weathered, and hauntingly beautiful. It is not just a ship; it is a relic of an age when the world was still being discovered, and the wind was the only engine of dreams.

name: Triaconter 30-Oared Ship - Stormworks
author: Thales
description: The Triaconter (Triakontoros, "Thirty-Oared") was one of the earliest and longest-serving Greek warship types, remaining in use from the Homeric Age to the campaigns of Alexander the Great. Propelled by 30 rowers and a single square sail, it was prized for its speed and versatility, serving in warfare, exploration, piracy, and trade. Later examples carried a bronze-sheathed ram for attacking enemy vessels. Among the most famous was the legendary Delias, the ship on which Theseus sailed to Crete to slay the Minotaur and rescue the Athenian youths.

name: Commemorative plaque - Jan Karel Zdenko Kotěra
author: 3dhdscan
description: Jan Karel Zdenko Kotěra (18th December 1871 Brno - 17th April 1923 Prague) was a Czech architect, urban designer, architect, furniture designer and painter. Kotěra was born in Brno, the largest city in Moravia, to a Czech father and German-speaking mother. He studied architecture in Vienna during the waning days of the Austro-Hungarian Empire under the Viennese master Otto Wagner. Kotěra returned to Prague in 1897 to help found a dynamic movement of Czech nationalist artists and architects centered on the Mánes Union of Fine Arts. Strongly influenced by the work of the Vienna Secession, his work bridged late nineteenth-century architectural design and early modernism. Kotěra collaborated with Czech sculptors Jan Štursa, Stanislav Sucharda, and Stanislav's son Vojtěch Sucharda on a number of buildings. As a teacher, Kotěra trained a generation of Czech architects, including Josef Gočár, who would bring Czech modernism to its pinnacle in the years leading up to the Nazi occupation in 1939.

name: Brass Leviathan - galleon
author: Brian Trepanier
description: Forged in the floating shipyards of Gearhold Bay, the Brass Leviathan was the crown jewel of the Aeronautic Armada, a galleon built not for war, but for wonder. Its hull, a fusion of aged timber and polished brass, houses a labyrinth of steam engines and gear-driven cannons. Legend says it was commissioned by the eccentric explorer Lady Virella, who sought to chart the skies above the Tempest Reaches. The ship’s figurehead, a brass muse with wind-swept hair, is said to whisper navigational secrets to the crew. Though its sails are worn and its pennants tattered, the Leviathan remains a beacon of steampunk ingenuity, an airborne relic of ambition, artistry, and adventure.

name: Ghost of the Seas - galleon
author: Brian Trepanier
description: Off the misty coast, a weathered galleon drifts silently, its towering masts slicing through the fog. Once a proud vessel of exploration and war, the ship now creaks with age, its sails faded to a ghostly white, fluttering like whispers of history. Built in the 1600s, this wooden giant carried gold, spices, and secrets across the treacherous oceans. Its hull, blackened by time and storm, still bears scars of cannon fire and salt. Barnacles cling to its flanks, and rope ladders sway gently in the breeze, untouched for decades. Legends surround the ship. Some say it vanished in a storm and returned untouched years later, its crew never found. Others claim to hear singing from its decks on quiet nights. Now, the galleon sits as a floating monument to an age of sails, salt, and shadow. It doesn’t speak—but if you listen close, the wind might carry its stories.

name: Queen Annes Revenge (FREE)
author: Mixmamo.studio:   An effortless 3D collections.
description: Model by Robert Ron Queen Anne’s Revenge is a legendary pirate ship 3D model inspired by the infamous flagship of Blackbeard (Edward Teach). This model captures the dark majesty of 18th-century naval warfare, blending historical authenticity with cinematic detail perfect for games or film environments. The ship features a heavily armed wooden hull, 32 iron cannons, ornate figurehead, and tattered black sails adorned with the iconic pirate insignia. The deck is richly detailed with ropes, barrels, lanterns, and weapon racks, while the captain’s cabin boasts aged wood textures, navigation charts, and gold accents that evoke the aura of fear and fortune. Built with modular design, the model allows easy customization — from clean museum-ready presentation to battle-worn realism. The Queen Anne’s Revenge sails again as a symbol of rebellion, terror, and the untamed spirit of the seas.

name: RSS Marrion
author: martyn169
description: RSS Marrion is an Ironclad fleet-cruiser built for the Svenberg navy. She and 7 others of her type were laid down in 4454 as part of a naval program to remove the aging wooden fleets and replace them with the newer and better Ironclads. Her main purpose was to serve along side capital ships in fleet operations and to take on the older tall ships of the line. The main 150mm guns could fire high explosive or semi armour piercing rounds, which would often tear through the weaker wooden ships outer hull and cause heavy damage inside. They still used sails and were 2 knots slower than the Krackens at 14 knots, however they could still outpace the older wooden ships, and even absorb allot of punishment in the process. The Marrion class as a whole would only last 20 years before being put in reserve before being scrapped a further 20 after that, however they did provide important lessons on how Iron cruisers could work.

name: Shipwreck 15563
author: BOEM Archaeology
description: This is the first model of shipwreck 15563. This was made using the high-resolution photogrammetry passes from Deep Discoverer (D2) remotely operated vehicle (ROV) on the Research Vessel Okeanos Explorer. These data were from NOAA Cruise EX2201 Dive 02. Much credit goes to the skillful ROV pilots on the Okeanos. Protocols for data collection and processing by BOEM’s Marine Archaeologist Scott Sorset. The BOEM Virtual Archaeology Museum can be accessed at https://www.boem.gov/Virtual-Archaeology-Museum/.

name: 1808 Kinman SBML 6 Pounder Cannon
author: Blair
description: This British Naval chase cannon mounted on field carriage is a smooth bore muzzle loaded ("SBML") 6 pounder. It has been on display in Britomart reserve, Akaroa New Zealand since 1907. Sometimes inaccurately identified as from the HMS Britomart, a Cherokee class brig-sloop, the cannon was sent to the 1906 international exhibition in Christchurch by the British admiralty as an example of the type of cannon similar to the two bow chasers on the HMS Britomart. Markings: Two crests appear on the barrel. On the first reinforce: Royal cypher of King George III. On the first reinforce ring is the mark of Francis Kinman of Woolwich, dated 1808. On the chase appears the cypher of the then Master General of the Ordinance (MGO), General John Pitt, 2nd Earl of Chatham. Both cyphers bear the motto "Honi soit qui mal y pense". On the third reinforce are the roman numerals DXXXVIII. On the right trunnion is the mark "No. 558".

name: Cannon
author: Evan16
description: This 3D model features a historical cannon, reminiscent of those used in the 18th and 19th centuries. The cannon is mounted on a robust wooden carriage, complete with four sturdy wheels, allowing for mobility on various terrains. The barrel of the cannon is made of cast iron, showcasing realistic textures and metallic reflections that emphasize its age and usage. The wooden carriage is meticulously detailed, displaying wood grain textures and a worn finish that suggests extensive use in historical battles or fort defenses. The iron cannon barrel includes subtle engravings and structural details, adding to the model's authenticity and historical accuracy. Perfect for historical reenactments, educational purposes, or as a prop in period-themed games and animations, this model brings a piece of history to life with detailed craftsmanship and realistic textures.

name: Brig Mahoning (Built 1847)
author: Wisconsin Shipwreck Coast NMS
description: MAHONING was built by William Jones in 1848 in Cleveland, OH, as a two-masted brig, measuring nearly 120 feet in length. Brigs are characterized as having two masts, outfit with square sails on both masts, and are relitively uncomon in the great Lakes. MAHONING spent most of its early sailing career transporting grain on the eastern Great Lakes, eventually moving to Lake Michigan, where it began hauling cargos of lumber to Chicago and Milwaukee. On November 4, 1864, MAHONING ran aground near the mouth of the Black River, just south of Sheboygan, during a gale. The vessel was successfully pulled off the beach, and slated to be towed to Milwaukee for repairs, however, on December 2, while enroute, MAHONING capsized south of Port Washington and was a total loss. Today, MAHONING sits in 55 feet of water, south of Port Washington. Despite the hull’s broken state, many construction components and a few artifacts remain, including the windlass, anchors, capstan, and carved figurehead. Data collected: 2022

name: Plaster mold for commemorative medal
author: Global Digital Heritage and GDH-Afrika
description: Plaster mold for the casting of the commemorative medal for the centenary of the heroine María Pita, defender of the city of La Coruña in 1589 against the English troops led by Sir Francis Drake. Only three medals were cast, all of them in silver, commissioned in 1890 by the “Liceo Brigantino” in La Coruña to commemorate the centenary. The piece is part of the Romero Ortiz Collection. 19th century. In the collection of the Spanish National Army Museum (Toledo, Spain). Catalog number MUE-25958. 3D model made using the Artec Space Spider scanner. Processing completed in Artec Studio Professional with additional processing completed in Geomagic Wrap. This work is part of the collaboration agreement signed in 2021 between the Ministry of Defence (Spain) and Global Digital Heritage (GDH) for the digitization of the collections preserved by the Spanish National Army Museum located in Toledo. We want to publicly thank the collaboration of all the museum staff, both civilian and military.

name: Uluburun, Bronze Age Merchant - Stormworks
author: Thales
description: A Canaanite merchant vessel sailed the eastern Mediterranean around 1300 BC, carrying one of the richest cargos ever found from the Bronze Age: ten tons of Cypriot copper, a ton of tin, Egyptian glass, ivory, gold, and luxury goods from across the Near East and Aegean. Bound most likely for a Mycenaean port, she sank off the rocky coast of Uluburun and lay undisturbed for over 3,300 years. Why the Uluburun Ship Matters It is the oldest known seagoing shipwreck with a largely intact cargo and the earliest clear evidence of advanced mortise-and-tenon hull construction. More than any other single discovery, Uluburun shows how deeply interconnected the Late Bronze Age world truly was — a floating crossroads of trade, diplomacy, and technology linking Cyprus, the Levant, Egypt, and the Aegean.

name: 3D Ship Model – Highly Detailed and Game-Ready
author: 1_floki_1
description: This 3D Ship model is a detailed, game-ready asset created for a wide range of digital projects. It combines realistic design, optimized geometry, and high-quality PBR textures, making it perfect for games, animations, VR/AR experiences, or cinematic scenes. The model has clean topology, balanced polycount, and comes in common formats such as FBX, OBJ, and BLEND for easy integration. Whether used as a central asset in a game level, a background element in a cinematic, or part of a VR/AR simulation, this ship adapts to different workflows.

name: Winifred Quigly (1753-69) Headstone
author: tippstudies
description: One of 240 memorials recorded in Old Terryglass graveyard (TN006-003008-), Co. Tipperary. 18th-century headstone marking the grave of Winifred Quigly (born c. 1753) who died in 1769 aged 16. Headstone erected by her father Garret Quigly. Inscription framed within a bevelled panel. Above the inscription there is the Cross-of-Thieves in an oval-shaped roundel. The upturned base of the central cross represents Golgotha or the mount on which Jesus was crucified. The "cross of thieves" refers to the crucifixion of Jesus alongside two criminals, described in the Gospels of Mark, Matthew, and particularly Luke, where one thief, the penitent thief, asked Jesus to remember him, and Jesus promised to bring him to paradise that day. The other thief, the impenitent thief, mocked Jesus, but the penitent thief rebuked him, acknowledging their just punishment and Jesus' innocence. For more details visit; https://historicgraves.com/terryglass-old-cemetery/tn-tygs-0167/grave

name: Churchclara: Walter O'Keeffe Stone
author: b-unicycling
description: This bullaun stone was described by Carrigan (1905) as a "holy water font" which had been carried "about a century ago" from the churchyard to the north of the churchyard. It is now on private land, but I had permission to scan it. Since Walter O'Keeffe carried it and challenged anyone to bring it back to the churchyard, it qualifies as a lifting stone. Carrigan writes that it weighs about 6cwt which makes it one of the heaviest in the country. Walter O'Keeffe died in October 18th 1752 aged 21 which dates his lift to before that date. SMR no.: KK020-017007- Made in KiriEngine from 77 images.

name: UNIT 3_Sura Acar
author: Horizon Arch Grad
description: The project area is located in İzmir/Mavişehir. The building to be constructed is a Waterfront center & Marina. Bringing together a marina, sailing and rowing club, hostel and a fisherman's cooperative, the project aims to connect with the urban environment and to revitalize the coastal area for citizens, serving as a social place. While designing the project, attention was paid to establishing a close relationship of the site with the sea and the river in general. Therefore, the site is located slightly above sea level. At the same time, there are areas on the sea-facing parts consisting of steps where people can spend time in close contact with the sea.
